author: Miguel Alfonso Caramoan
title: Nikola Jokic looks to rediscover his rhythm against Indiana Pacers on ESPN on Disney+ - NewsBreak
text:
By Miguel Alfonso Caramoan ,
1 hours ago
There is a peculiar challenge that comes with being Nikola Jokic. When you have spent the better part of a decade making the extraordinary look ordinary, even a relatively modest dip in production can become a talking point.
For most NBA players, averaging 23.4 points, 9.7 rebounds and 9.3 assists through seven games represents an outstanding start to a season. For Jokic, it feels a little different. The three-time MVP has spent years operating at a level where a triple-double is almost an expectation rather than an accomplishment, and where his efficiency has become just as important as his ability to fill the box score.
As the league marks its 35th NBA Mexico Game, Jokic and the Denver Nuggets look to reestablish him as one of the best players in the world when they take on the struggling Indiana Pacers at the Arena CDMX in Mexico City.
Watch Nikola Jokic and the Denver Nuggets play the Indiana Pacers in the NBA Mexico City Game 2026 on ESPN on Disney+ Philippines on Sunday, Nov. 8 from 6 a.m. (PST)
The numbers behind Jokic's early-season shooting struggles are difficult to ignore. Through seven games, he is converting just 50.4% of his field-goal attempts and 21.9% of his three-pointers, a notable dip from the 56.9% shooting clip and 38% from beyond the arc he posted last season.
In fact, his struggles from the perimeter have become particularly noticeable for a player who has consistently used his shooting touch to keep opposing defenses honest. Jokic's ability to score inside and create for others remains intact, but the reduced effectiveness of his outside shot is giving defenses more room to adjust their coverage.
"I don't know why, but when I'm shooting them and practicing them, I'm kind of making it," Jokic said after the Nuggets' 118-110 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers on Tuesday.
"But I'm not making it in the game. But I think the struggle, it's a privilege."
Jokic and the Nuggets can, however, take encouragement from their most recent outing, against Toronto Raptors on Thursday, when the 31-year old center delivered arguably his most complete performance of the young season. Jokic posted 32 points, 10 rebounds and 11 assists in a 128-109 victory, shooting an impressive 13-of-19 from the field.
The Pacers, meanwhile, are looking to find their footing after dealing with multiple injuries.
They have endured a brutal stretch to open November, losing five consecutive games before getting back into the win column with a 107-103 victory over the previously undefeated Memphis Grizzlies. Their injury problems have been so severe that they had only six players available for their 108-104 loss to the Atlanta Hawks on Nov. 3, an extraordinary situation that exposed just how thin their rotation had become.
There is some positive news for the Pacers as they have a possible answer to the Jokic question. Ivica Zubac returned to the starting lineup against Memphis after missing five games with a left ankle sprain, giving the Pacers a much-needed interior presence ahead of their matchup with one of the league's most dominant centers. Obi Toppin also returned, although Indiana remains without several key contributors, including Tyrese Haliburton and T.J. McConnell.
For Jokic, the matchup presents another opportunity to build on his performance against Toronto and show that his early-season shooting struggles are nothing more than a temporary hurdle. With Zubac back in the fold, Indiana has a better chance of challenging him inside, but slowing the Serbian superstar will require more than just a strong individual defensive effort.
Both teams have something to prove in Mexico City, but the spotlight will focus most sharply on Jokic as he looks to show he's still on top of his game.
